source_evidence.observation: For a matrix M, |M| is defined entrywise as (|m_ij|); subsequent absolute-value matrix inequalities therefore have componentwise meaning.

source_evidence.anchor: block-FMA model, equations (2.3)-(2.6), and gamma notation
source_evidence.observation: The block-FMA output precision u_FMA is either u_low or u_high; C+AB is evaluated at internal precision bar_u <= u_FMA and then rounded to u_FMA. The scalar model is fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta), equivalently (a op b)/(1+delta), with |delta|<=u. The paper defines gamma_k=ku/(1-ku), bar_gamma_k=k*bar_u/(1-k*bar_u), and tilde_gamma_k^FMA=k*tilde_u_FMA/(1-k*tilde_u_FMA), assuming the relevant k times each unit roundoff is less than 1.

Algorithm 3.1 converts multiplicands to u_low when necessary, chains block FMAs, and returns the result in working precision u. The analysis explicitly assumes that underflow and overflow do not occur, although scaling may be needed in an implementation.

The effective outer-rounding unit roundoff is tilde_u_FMA=u if u>u_FMA, 0 if bar_u>=u_FMA, and u_FMA if bar_u<u_FMA, with the first case taking precedence when conditions overlap. If u>u_FMA>bar_u, two roundings occur, but the analysis retains only one and calls the effect of double rounding negligible.

Algorithm 4.1 is a right-looking block LU factorization of A in R^(n x n), with b x b blocks and q=n/b integral. A is given in working precision u; diagonal factorizations and block triangular solves use u; update operands are converted to u_low and the trailing updates use Algorithm 3.1 and a b x b FMA. No pivot or permutation operation is displayed.

Lemma 4.2 supplies componentwise LU and triangular-solve error models with gamma_b. Theorem 4.3 gives the factorization-stage perturbation coefficient 2*u_low+u_low^2+max(tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA+bar_gamma_(n-b+1)+tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA*bar_gamma_(n-b+1),gamma_b)*(1+u_low)^2, multiplying |A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)|.

If Algorithm 4.1 produces computed factors hat(L), hat(U), and substitution produces hat(x) for Ax=b, then (A+Delta A)hat(x)=b. Equation (4.7) adds 2*gamma_n+gamma_n^2 to the complete factorization-stage coefficient and multiplies the entire coefficient by |A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)|. The proof combines Theorem 4.3 with triangular-system solution error analysis.

binders: First fix A in R^(n x n), a b x b block partition, and q=n/b with q an integer. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

Inherited precision parameters are working unit roundoff u, conversion unit roundoff u_low, block-FMA choices u_low and u_high, block-FMA output unit roundoff u_FMA, internal unit roundoff bar_u, and effective outer-rounding unit roundoff tilde_u_FMA. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 4/C127, block-FMA model; PDF p. 6/C129, (3.3)]

Conditionally bind the computed factors hat(L), hat(U) produced by Algorithm 4.1 and the computed solution hat(x) produced by substitution for Ax=b_rhs; only after these outputs are available does the conclusion introduce a coefficient perturbation Delta A. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

The dimensions hat(L), hat(U), Delta A in R^(n x n) and hat(x), b_rhs in R^n are inferred from the displayed products and Ax=b; Theorem 4.4 does not separately state the vector dimensions. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and (4.7)]
hypotheses: A is partitioned into square b x b blocks and q=n/b is an integer. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

A is supplied in working precision u; Algorithm 4.1's diagonal block factorizations and triangular solves use precision u, while its update path uses the mixed-precision block FMA. [PDF p. 11/C134, section 4 precision paragraph and Algorithm 4.1]

Algorithm 4.1 actually produces computed LU factors and the subsequent substitution actually yields a computed solution; the theorem is conditional on success rather than on an explicit nonsingularity or no-breakdown criterion. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
For every gamma quantity used, the corresponding index times its underlying unit roundoff is less than 1. [PDF p. 4/C127, gamma paragraph]
Underflow and overflow are excluded by the inherited Algorithm 3.1 analysis. [PDF p. 5/C128, paragraph following Algorithm 3.1]
conclusions: There is a coefficient perturbation Delta A such that (A+Delta A)hat(x)=b_rhs; the right-hand side is the same b_rhs as in Ax=b_rhs. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

Componentwise, |Delta A| <= c*(|A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)|), where c=2*u_low+u_low^2+max(tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA+bar_gamma_(n-b+1)+tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA*bar_gamma_(n-b+1),gamma_b)*(1+u_low)^2+2*gamma_n+gamma_n^2. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
definitions_and_conventions: |M| means entrywise absolute value, so the bound and all intermediate absolute-value inequalities are componentwise. [PDF p. 3/C126, matrix absolute-value definition]

gamma_k=k*u/(1-k*u), bar_gamma_k=k*bar_u/(1-k*bar_u), and tilde_gamma_k^FMA=k*tilde_u_FMA/(1-k*tilde_u_FMA). An accent on gamma transfers to its unit roundoff, and the FMA superscript transfers to the unit-roundoff subscript. [PDF p. 4/C127, gamma notation]
u_FMA is either u_low or u_high, while bar_u is the precision used internally to evaluate C+AB before the result is rounded to u_FMA. [PDF p. 4/C127, block-FMA model before (2.3)]

tilde_u_FMA is defined by the ordered cases in (3.3): u when u>u_FMA; otherwise 0 when bar_u>=u_FMA; otherwise u_FMA when bar_u<u_FMA. [PDF p. 6/C129, equation (3.3) and following precedence sentence]

Hats denote computed factors or solutions; tildes in Algorithm 4.1 and its proof denote computed factors converted to u_low. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1 line 8; PDF p. 12/C135, proof of Theorem 4.3]
implicit_context: The displayed algorithm is unpivoted in the literal sense that it contains no pivot search, row interchange, or permutation matrix, although the theorem does not separately say 'without pivoting.' [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1]
The phrase 'substitution' is not expanded into pseudocode in Theorem 4.4; its proof invokes the standard error analysis for triangular-system solution. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 proof]

The perturbation in Theorem 4.4 is a combined factorization-plus-solve perturbation and need not be identified with the Delta A symbol used locally in Theorem 4.3. [PDF p. 12/C135, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 proof]
The theorem is general and does not specialize to tensor-core values b=4, u_low=u16, or u_high=u32. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4; tensor-core specialization begins after its proof]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is specifically linked to the right-looking block LU Algorithm 4.1: factor each diagonal block, solve for the current block column and row, convert update operands to u_low, and update trailing blocks through Algorithm 3.1's block-FMA path; substitution is then applied to the computed factors. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
numerical_model: Scalar operations obey fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta), equivalently (a op b)/(1+delta), with |delta|<=the relevant unit roundoff and op in {+,-,multiplication,division}. [PDF p. 4/C127, equations (2.3)-(2.4)]
For one b x b block FMA, the paper's model is |hat(D)-D|<=u_FMA*|hat(D)|+bar_gamma_(b+1)*(|C|+|A||B|). [PDF p. 4/C127, equations (2.5)-(2.6)]

Conversions satisfy tilde(L)_ij=hat(L)_ij+E_ij and tilde(U)_jk=hat(U)_jk+F_jk with |E_ij|<=u_low|hat(L)_ij| and |F_jk|<=u_low|hat(U)_jk|; these produce the terms 2*u_low+u_low^2 and the factor (1+u_low)^2. [PDF p. 12/C135, proof of Theorem 4.3]

The triangular-solve model is T*hat(X)=B+Delta B with |Delta B|<=gamma_b|T||hat(X)| for a nonsingular b x b triangular T; Theorem 4.4 applies the corresponding n-dimensional solve analysis. [PDF p. 12/C135, Lemma 4.2 equation (4.3); PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 proof]
When the implementation would round first to u_FMA and then to a coarser working precision u, the derivation models only one rounding. [PDF p. 6/C129, paragraph before (3.2)]
error_notions: The conclusion is a componentwise backward error in the coefficient matrix: the computed hat(x) exactly solves a nearby system with A replaced by A+Delta A. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and (4.7)]
No perturbation of b_rhs is present in the final nearby-system equation. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
The mandatory scale is |A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)|, not |A| alone. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
No forward-error, relative-residual, or normwise-error conclusion is stated. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and (4.7)]
norms: No matrix or vector norm occurs in Theorem 4.4; vertical bars denote componentwise absolute values. [PDF p. 3/C126, absolute-value convention; PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]

In |hat(L)||hat(U)|, juxtaposition is ordinary matrix multiplication of the two nonnegative entrywise-absolute-value matrices, not an entrywise product. [PDF p. 3/C126, convention; PDF p. 13/C136, dimensionally conforming scale in (4.7)]
constants_and_indexing: The update term uses exactly q-1 and n-b+1: tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA+bar_gamma_(n-b+1)+their product. These offsets must not be replaced by q or n. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
The max is exactly between the complete update term and gamma_b, and only that max is multiplied by (1+u_low)^2. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
The solve contribution +2*gamma_n+gamma_n^2 is outside the max but inside the overall scalar coefficient. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
The whole scalar coefficient multiplies the whole scale |A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)|. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
Algorithm 4.1 indexes block loops from 1 through q. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1]
higher_order_terms: Equation (4.7) retains u_low^2, the product tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA*bar_gamma_(n-b+1), the square (1+u_low)^2, and gamma_n^2. [PDF p. 13/C136, equation (4.7)]
Theorem 4.4 has no omitted O-term and is not merely the first-order or dominant-term table specialization. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and (4.7)]

Separately, the block-FMA discussion says that setting bar_u=0 represents a rounded-exact FMA only to within O(u_FMA^2), because |hat(D)| rather than |D| appears in (2.6); this O-statement is not an extra term in (4.7). [PDF p. 4/C127, paragraph following (2.6)]
The possible second rounding described in Algorithm 3.1 is omitted rather than represented by an explicit higher-order remainder in (4.7). [PDF p. 6/C129, paragraph before (3.2)]
exceptional_values: The inherited matrix-multiplication analysis assumes that neither underflow nor overflow occurs. [PDF p. 5/C128, paragraph following Algorithm 3.1]
NaNs, infinities, subnormal behavior, and division-by-zero behavior are not separately specified in the cited model or theorem. [PDF p. 4/C127, equations (2.3)-(2.6); PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
Factorization breakdown or failure of substitution is handled only by the conditional wording that the algorithm produces factors and substitution yields a solution. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

undebatable_constraints: The result must include both (A+Delta A)hat(x)=b_rhs and the componentwise bound on |Delta A|. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and (4.7)]
The coefficient must contain every term: 2*u_low, u_low^2, the max term, (1+u_low)^2, 2*gamma_n, and gamma_n^2. [PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]

The accents are semantically essential: the update uses tilde_gamma^FMA and bar_gamma, while block factorization and substitution use unaccented gamma_b and gamma_n. [PDF p. 4/C127, gamma convention; PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]
The exact indices are q-1, n-b+1, b, and n. [PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]
The factor |A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)| is mandatory and lies outside the complete coefficient. [PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]
The bound is componentwise, not normwise, and the right-hand side is unperturbed. [PDF p. 3/C126, absolute-value convention; PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
The theorem is conditional on successful Algorithm 4.1 factor production and successful substitution. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
No first-order simplification, tensor-core specialization, or big-O replacement is equivalent to the exact source claim. [PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]

ambiguities.issue: The symbol b is used both for the scalar block size and for the right-hand-side vector in Ax=b. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem states a b x b partition with q=n/b and later writes Ax=b and (A+Delta A)hat(x)=b without typographically renaming either occurrence. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must distinguish block size from the RHS vector, but the source does not supply separate names; the RHS dimension R^n is inferred. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

ambiguities.issue: The exact substitution algorithm is not specified. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
ambiguities.evidence: The statement says only that 'substitution' yields hat(x), and the proof refers to triangular-system error analysis. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and proof]
ambiguities.impact: Forward and backward triangular substitution are strongly suggested by LU, but no separate pseudocode, ordering, or precision declaration for substitution appears in the theorem. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 13/C136, proof]

ambiguities.issue: Algorithm 4.1 has an apparent index inconsistency in its conversion line. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1 lines 7-9]
ambiguities.evidence: Inside loops over i and j, line 8 displays conversion of U_ki, while line 9 uses tilde(U)_kj in the A_ij update. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1 lines 7-9]
ambiguities.impact: The likely intended conversion is U_kj, as used by the update and subsequent proof, but the literal displayed pseudocode should not be silently rewritten without recording this discrepancy. [PDF p. 11/C134, line 9; PDF p. 12/C135, proof of Theorem 4.3]

ambiguities.issue: The treatment of an actual two-step rounding is deliberately simplified. [PDF p. 6/C129, paragraph before (3.2)]
ambiguities.evidence: For u>u_FMA>bar_u the paper says two roundings are required but includes only one in the analysis, describing the effect as negligible. [PDF p. 6/C129, paragraph before (3.2)]
ambiguities.impact: Equation (4.7) is exact for the stated analytical model, not a fully explicit bound containing both physical rounding steps. [PDF p. 6/C129, rounding simplification; PDF p. 13/C136, (4.7)]

ambiguities.issue: No explicit nonsingularity, pivot condition, or leading-principal-minor condition is stated for A. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem instead assumes conditionally that Algorithm 4.1 produces factors and substitution yields a solution; Algorithm 4.1 displays no pivoting. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]
ambiguities.impact: Successful completion must remain a hypothesis; it cannot be replaced silently by a stronger or different structural condition on A. [PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4]

ambiguities.issue: The cited passages specify the standard relative-error model but do not explicitly name an IEEE tie-breaking rounding mode. [PDF p. 4/C127, equations (2.3)-(2.6)]
ambiguities.evidence: The text says operations and FMA outputs are rounded to stated precisions and gives unit-roundoff bounds, without stating a tie rule in this passage. [PDF p. 4/C127, block-FMA and scalar models]
ambiguities.impact: The contract supports the displayed relative-error assumptions but not an additional claim such as round-to-nearest-ties-to-even unless supplied from outside the authorized passage. [PDF p. 4/C127, equations (2.3)-(2.6)]

contract_plain_english: For an n x n matrix A partitioned into b x b blocks with integral q=n/b, condition on the unpivoted displayed block-LU Algorithm 4.1 actually producing computed factors and on substitution producing hat(x). Then there exists a coefficient perturbation Delta A for which hat(x) exactly solves (A+Delta A)hat(x)=b_rhs. Componentwise, |Delta A| is bounded by |A|+|hat(L)||hat(U)| times the full coefficient 2*u_low+u_low^2+max(tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA+bar_gamma_(n-b+1)+tilde_gamma_(q-1)^FMA*bar_gamma_(n-b+1),gamma_b)*(1+u_low)^2+2*gamma_n+gamma_n^2. The RHS is not perturbed, no normwise or forward-error claim is made, and none of the squared or product terms may be dropped. The claim uses the paper's standard relative-error and block-FMA models, assumes the relevant gamma denominators are valid and excludes underflow and overflow. [PDF p. 11/C134, Algorithm 4.1; PDF p. 13/C136, Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.7); PDF p. 4/C127, equations (2.3)-(2.6); PDF p. 5/C128, no-underflow/no-overflow assumption]
